rows.note: Use this all-purpose noun construction for a sudden burst or outflow of a liquid or other flowing substance, such as 一股水.

example.english: A gush of water suddenly burst out of the pipe.
example.jyutping: seoi2 hau4 dat6 jin4 jung2 ceot1 jat1 gu2 seoi2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when liquid or another substance flows out suddenly in a large volume.

example.english: When the pipe bursts, water can gush out all at once.
example.traditional: 條水喉爆裂，啲水即刻湧出嚟。
example.jyutping: tiu4 seoi2 hau4 baau3 lit6 di1 seoi2 zik1 hak1 jung2 ceot1 lai4

rows.note: Use this when a person, object, or opening actively sends liquid or another substance out suddenly and forcefully.

example.english: The pump can make water gush out.
example.traditional: 個水泵一開，就可以將啲水噴出嚟。
example.jyutping: go3 seoi2 bam1 jat1 hoi1 zau6 ho2 ji5 zoeng1 di1 seoi2 pan3 ceot1 lai4

rows.note: Use this when someone keeps praising a person or thing with excessive enthusiasm, rather than when something physically flows out.

example.english: After trying the restaurant’s signature dish, they gush with praise.
example.traditional: 佢食完嗰間餐廳嘅招牌菜，就讚不絕口。
example.jyutping: keoi5 sik6 jyun4 go2 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 ziu1 paai4 coi3 zau6 zaan3 bat1 zyut6 hau2
